themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked to 48 THIS WEEK compared to a 11.6-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 313% increase (z-score: 5.94)—suggesting either new venues opening, construction activity, or enforcement gaps in Sunset Park's mixed-use corridors.
evidence: 48 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Active ULURP applications (364 Coney Island Ave, 783 Fourth Ave) suggest ongoing commercial/mixed-use development
reporting_angles: Which new bars, restaurants, or music venues opened recently in Sunset Park—and are noise permits in place?
Are construction projects (tied to rezoning applications) running evening shifts without proper permits?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints surged to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 1233% increase (z-score: 9.55, highest severity)—indicating a serious and localized public safety concern that may be worsening.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
1233% spike with z-score of 9.55 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Related spike: Drinking complaints up 273% (7 last week vs. 1.9 avg) and Smoking/Vaping up 300% (3 this week vs. 0.8 avg), suggesting coordinated street-level disorder
reporting_angles: Which neighborhoods/blocks are the epicenters of drug activity—and what enforcement response has NYPD mounted?
Are community board street outreach requests (budgeted annually but apparently unfunded) leaving vulnerable blocks unmonitored?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Street Disorder Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints hit 30 THIS WEEK versus an 8.2-per-week baseline—a 264% spike (z-score: 3.09)—converging with elevated noise, drug activity, and drinking complaints to paint a picture of deteriorating street conditions and possible enforcement gaps.
evidence: 30 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Clustering with drug activity, drinking, and commercial noise spikes suggests broader street-disorder outbreak, not isolated issue
reporting_angles: Are tagging crews targeting specific areas (near Sunset Park Greenway or new commercial zones)?
What is the DSNY/Parks Dept response time for graffiti removal—and are crews overwhelmed?

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.1-per-week average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, high severity)—possibly reflecting illegal street vending, permit violations, or health/sanitation complaints tied to unregulated operators.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
May correlate with Sunset Park Greenway opening (May 7, 2026) drawing foot traffic and illegal operators
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food carts clustering near the new Sunset Park Greenway, and what health violations have been cited?
How is NYC Dept. of Consumer Affairs enforcing mobile vending permits in this district?

themes_detail.label: Boiler/Heat System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 0.2-per-week baseline—a 1100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—converging with the broader Heat/Hot Water complaint trend (784 complaints over 90 days) to signal systemic heating infrastructure failures as cold season peaks.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Heat/Hot Water is second-largest complaint category overall (784 over 90 days), indicating systemic problem beyond temporary spike
reporting_angles: Which residential buildings have chronic boiler failures—and what are landlord response times under HPD oversight?
Are aging housing stock in Sunset Park (many pre-1960s buildings per budget requests for NYCHA upgrades) failing at higher rates than citywide average?
